$comment: PRD_FOOD 9.5 turned into rules. Everything here is mechanical and applies to the
whole table; the handful of decisions a rule cannot make live in
subset.overrides.json, where they can be reviewed one line at a time.
`bun run catalogue:report` prints what each pass removed, so a change to this file
shows up as a diff in counts rather than as a silently different catalogue.
targetSizeComment: The reviewed intent, not a constraint the build enforces. The report prints the
actual size against it and says so loudly when it falls outside, because a subset
that quietly doubled is the failure worth catching. It does not fail the build: the
size is a consequence of Ciqual's contents and of the rules below, and a build that
refused to run would only invite someone to widen the window.
subGroupAllowlistComment: Ciqual's own sub-groups, kept when the module would log the food and dropped when
Group 11 (baby food) is out entirely: PRD_FOOD addresses an adult logging what they
ate. Most of group 01 (composed dishes) is out because a lasagne is what PRD_FOOD
9.2's barcode scan or 11's recipes are for; soups stay because they are eaten as
themselves. Group 10 keeps sauces and plant-based spreads and drops cooking aids,
salts, spices and herbs, which nobody logs and which would crowd every search.
The same 9.2 argument removes the sub-groups that are almost entirely packaged
products with a barcode on them: savoury biscuits (0303), fish products i.e. surimi
and breaded fillets (0409), non-chocolate confectionery (0703), sweet biscuits
(0706), breakfast cereals (0707), cereal bars (0708), ice cream (0801) and sorbet
(0802). A generic 'sweet biscuit' row is a worse answer than the scan of the packet
in the user's hand. Cakes and pastries (0705, 0709) stay, because those are also
baked at home and bought unwrapped.
subSubGroupDenylistComment: Whole sub-sub-groups removed inside an otherwise allowed sub-group.
enumerates the produce of two French overseas departments separately from the same
produce grown anywhere else, which is 83 rows that differ by where the plant grew.
040305 to 040309 are pates, rillettes, quenelles, 'other delicatessen' and
plant-based delicatessen; 040108 and 040208 are offals. Both are foods someone
eats, and both are long tails of near-identical rows that would take a fifth of the
catalogue. They are the first thing to put back if the catalogue has room.
020103 is dried and dehydrated vegetables, 060207 is drink powders to reconstitute:
in both, the shipped figures describe the powder and the user would weigh the drink.
clusterByComment: The unit PRD_FOOD 9.5's 15 % is applied inside, per sub-group. The default,
`headNoun`, is right almost everywhere; see src/subset.ts for why the sub-group
`subGroup` for the four fish and seafood sub-groups: Ciqual lists 108 raw fish and
bogue, megrim and pond smelt are three head nouns with one set of numbers.
`subSubGroup` where Ciqual's own sub-sub-group already names a kind of food rather
than a state of one - 'beef and veal', 'hard or pressed cheeses', 'juices'. It is
deliberately *not* used for vegetables, fruits, legumes, eggs or grains, whose
sub-sub-groups say raw/cooked: clustering those whole deletes the cauliflower and
millilitreSubGroupsComment: PRD_FOOD 8.6: a liquid says so explicitly and Mue applies no density. Only the
sub-groups whose contents are drunk are listed. Oils are deliberately absent: they
are sold by volume, but density 0,92 is exactly the implicit conversion 8.6 forbids,
and Ciqual states them per 100 g.
excludePatternsComment: PRD_FOOD 9.5's three unjustified separations, plus 9.2's division of labour with the
barcode scan. Each pattern is a JavaScript regular expression tested against
alim_nom_eng, case-insensitively unless it says otherwise.

excludePatterns.reason: a capitalised parenthetical names a brand or a spring - codes 76000..76049 are fifty bottled waters written this way. Case-sensitive on purpose: read case-insensitively it also matches Ciqual's own '(average)' rows, which are the generic entries this file works hardest to keep
PRD_FOOD 9.2 gives packaged products to the barcode scan; 533 Ciqual rows are marked this way and each is an industrial formulation, not a generic food
a list of springs, i.e. of brands
a serving instruction, not a food

requireEnergyComment: PRD_FOOD 9.3 accepts a personal food with no values, because an Open Food Facts
record is often incomplete and the user can fill it in. A shipped catalogue row is
different: nobody can complete it, it can never contribute to a total, and it
occupies a line of every search result it matches.
clusteringComment: PRD_FOOD 9.5: 'deux entrees distinctes ne se justifient que si leurs valeurs
different de plus d'environ 15 %'. The floor is the source's own resolution: Ciqual
writes raw white rice fat as 0,79, and 15 % of that is 0,12 g, which is noise rather
than a difference anyone could notice in a logged meal.
cookedRatioComment: PRD_FOOD 8.6's raw/cooked test. `gating` is the list of constituents allowed to
refuse a pair; see the RescaleTolerance doc comment in src/pairing.ts for why fibre
is measured, reported and not allowed to vote.
